objective.value: Design, construct and tune bifunctional (positive- and negative-response) glycolysis-flux biosensors based on the Cra-FBP pair that sense intracellular fructose-1,6-diphosphate (FBP) and dynamically regulate glycolysis flux, then apply them to balance biosynthesis of mevalonate (MVA) and N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) in Escherichia coli.
objective.notes: Abstract explicitly states design/construction of bifunctional glycolysis flux biosensor and application to MVA and GlcNAc.

hypothesis.value: Because intracellular FBP concentration is linearly related to glycolysis flux (via FBP feedforward activation of pyruvate kinase), a Cra/FBP-based transcriptional biosensor can report flux in vivo and drive autonomous, timely dynamic repression/activation of pathway genes, outperforming static knockout and IPTG-induced CRISPRi control.

inference.rationale: Introduction (1_introduction_p003) presents the FBP-flux linear relationship (cited to Kochanowski et al. 2013, a background_citation) as the premise; Results compare dynamic control against permanent pfkA deletion and cite Li et al. 2021 CRISPRi as inferior, implying the tested hypothesis.

hypothesis.notes: The FBP-flux linearity premise itself is attributed to prior literature (background_citation), not newly demonstrated by this paper except via the deficiency-strain validation experiment.

outcomes.value: Tuned negative-response biosensor pL19 detects intracellular FBP over ~0-50 mmol/g DCW, covering the reported physiological 0-31 mM/g DCW range; fluorescence of BW-pfkA, BW-ptsG, BW-pykF was 11.32, 7.13, 1.11x BW25113 at 18 h (order BW-pfkA > BW-ptsG > BW-pykF > BW25113). MVA: BW-PR produced 73.31 g/L MVA in shake flask (carbon yield 63.00 mol%, highest shake-flask MVA to date per authors) with <0.1 g/L acetate and no other byproducts; BW-PMT <2.47 g/L acetate; 111.3 g/L MVA after 120 h in 1-L fermenter with no by-products. GlcNAc: DN5-IM 8.65 g/L vs DN5 0.46 g/L; DN5-GM 6.33 and DN5-GAR 7.98 g/L; DN5-IMM 8.63 g/L; simultaneous pfkA repression + glmS activation gave no obvious titer increase over single regulation. Dynamic control outperformed IPTG-CRISPRi benchmark (8.53 g/L, Li et al. 2021; 0.12x of BW-PR).
outcomes.notes: Author claims ('highest to date', 'timely and gradually blocked') are author_interpretation; titer numbers are direct_observations bound to stated strains/conditions.

experiments.purpose: Create and tune positive-response FBP biosensors (pL01-pL10; refined pL15-pL18) with varied thresholds/dynamic ranges.

interventions.description: Promoter-architecture engineering of Cra-regulated promoters (core promoter strength, TFBS position, Cra-box sequence) to build pL01-pL10 and refined pL15-pL18.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes (de novo promoter circuit construction), Q2 yes (this study), Q3 yes (variants with distinct thresholds enabled later selection of Ppam/PM23107 for applications).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Construction of metabolite-responsive dynamic regulation components (sensor-regulator).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Few biosensors exist for central glycolytic metabolites; glycolysis flux imbalance (overflow at high flux, poor growth at low flux) lacks autonomous regulation systems.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Dose-response curves measured in vivo and Hill-fitted (Fig. 2A,C,E).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Design based on stated transcription-regulation equilibrium among FBP, Cra and operator DNA (4_discussion_p004), i.e., explicit mechanistic basis.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When building an FBP/Cra-based glycolysis-flux sensor in E. coli, tune core promoter strength, TFBS position and Cra-box affinity so the sensor threshold and dynamic range span the physiological intracellular FBP range, because sensor output is set by the FBP-Cra-DNA equilibrium. (Validated only for Cra/FBP biosensors in E. coli in this paper.)

interventions.description: Tuning by Cra overexpression and by mutating Cra ligand-binding affinity (positive-response branch, Fig. 2B).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Deliberate modification of regulator level/affinity to shift sensor response; informs tunability claims.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Regulator-level tuning of the dynamic control circuit.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Initial promoter variants did not cover desired thresholds/dynamic ranges (implied by need for further tuning axes).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Resulting sensors characterized by measured dose-response (Fig. 2C,E).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Affinity/expression-level changes act on the Cra-FBP-DNA equilibrium, as explicitly reasoned in Discussion.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a TF-based metabolite sensor's threshold is mismatched to the in vivo effector range in E. coli, adjust regulator expression level or ligand-binding affinity of the TF, because both shift the occupancy equilibrium of the operator. (Validated for Cra/FBP in E. coli only.)
alternatives_considered: Cra-overexpressing plasmid sensors were later excluded from application cases because of Cra's global regulatory impact (4_discussion_p004).

interventions.description: Promoter engineering to convert Cra regulation into negative-response output (pL19-pL30); site mutagenesis of Cra at amino acids 57-60 under P23102 (pL35).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: New circuit construction plus rationally placed TF mutations; pL19/pL25 later selected for pfkA control.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Need to down-regulate glycolysis (pfkA) autonomously when FBP (flux proxy) is high; positive-response sensors alone cannot repress.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured dose-response curves and Hill fits (Fig. 3A,C); pL35 characterized by dose-response (Fig. 3B).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: TFBS position and TF structural changes alter regulation mode (4_discussion_p006) - mechanistic reasoning given by authors.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a pathway gene must be repressed at high glycolysis flux in E. coli, place Cra TFBS so that FBP-bound Cra relieves/reorganizes repression to yield negative FBP-response, and tune via Cra ligand-affinity mutations, because regulation sign and dose-response are set by TFBS position and TF-ligand affinity. (Validated for Cra-based circuits in E. coli only.)

experiments.purpose: Replace static pfkA knockout in the EP-bifido pathway with FBP-responsive dynamic repression to resolve growth/production trade-off and maximize MVA.

interventions.description: Genomic replacement of the zwf promoter with the stronger P23109 promoter (strain BW-Pzwf::P23109).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes (promoter replacement this study), Q2 yes (performed here on the EP-bifido background), Q3 yes (creates the base strain onto which dynamic pfkA control is layered).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Enhancing PP pathway entry (G6P dehydrogenase, Zwf) to supply fructose-6-phosphate and NADPH for the EP-bifido route.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Prior EP-bifido design (Wang et al. 2019) requires sufficient F6P and NADPH supply from the PP pathway; natural glycolysis was previously blocked by permanent pfkA deletion.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Resulting strain phenotypes (growth, glucose uptake, MVA) measured in this study.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Rationale explicitly stated: stronger zwf promoter enhances PP pathway flux for F6P/NADPH supply (stoichiometric/pathway mechanism).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When an EP-bifido-type acetyl-CoA/F6P supply pathway in E. coli is limited by PP pathway throughput, up-regulate zwf via a stronger constitutive promoter, because Zwf controls carbon entry into the PP pathway that delivers F6P and NADPH. (Validated for MVA production in this E. coli EP-bifido system.)

interventions.description: Genomic replacement of the pfkA promoter with negative-response biosensor promoters Ppam (pL19) or Ppar (pL25), yielding BW-PMT and BW-PR (dynamic EP-bifido pathway).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes (genomic promoter replacement), Q2 yes (this study), Q3 yes (two thresholds compared; Ppar selected as superior, guiding the final strain).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Metabolite-responsive dynamic down-regulation of a competing glycolysis step.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Permanent pfkA deletion severely suppressed growth and glucose uptake, capping MVA at 11.02 g/L despite 64.3 mol% yield - a measured growth/production trade-off demanding dynamic instead of static control.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titers, growth, mRNA and FBP time courses for BW-PMT/BW-PR vs non-regulated control.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic logic explicit: sense FBP (flux proxy) to repress pfkA only after growth phase, switching flux into EP-bifido and uncoupling growth from production.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When static knockout of an essential glycolytic step (e.g., pfkA) in E. coli collapses growth and substrate uptake, replace the native promoter with a biosensor promoter negatively responsive to intracellular FBP, because FBP reports glycolytic flux and enables automatic growth-then-production switching. (Validated for MVA via EP-bifido in E. coli; extended to GlcNAc in EXP5.)
alternatives_considered: IPTG-induced CRISPRi repression of pfkA (Li et al. 2021) - external-inducer strategy; yielded only 8.53 g/L MVA (0.12x of BW-PR) and requires inducer timing; cited as inferior benchmark (background_citation).

interventions.description: Scale-up fermentation of BW-PR in a 1-L fermenter.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q3 not passed: fermentation of the already-selected BW-PR evaluates performance at scale without introducing a new design modification.

experiments.conditions: Shake flask; 1-L fermenter 120 h; feeding/medium unknown (Methods absent; Supplementary Figs. 6-7 not available).
experiments.controls: Non-regulated BW-Pzwf::P23109; prior static-knockout BW-delta-pfkA EP-bifido (background_citation benchmark, Wang et al. 2019); IPTG-CRISPRi strain (background_citation benchmark, Li et al. 2021).
experiments.readouts: MVA titer and carbon yield; growth; glucose uptake; acetate/byproducts; pfkA mRNA; intracellular FBP.
experiments.analysis: Time-course comparison of growth/production; mRNA and FBP trends as dynamic-control confirmation.
experiments.outcome: BW-PR: 73.31 g/L MVA, 63.00 mol% carbon yield, <0.1 g/L acetate, stationary phase after 12 h, FBP drop after 15 h; fermenter: 111.3 g/L at 120 h, no by-products. BW-PMT accumulated <2.47 g/L acetate.
experiments.scope_notes: Dynamic-regulation claims supported within tested conditions only; mRNA/FBP confirmation is correlative to promoter replacement (no inducer-timing sweep shown in main text).

experiments.purpose: Balance glycolysis and GlcNAc biosynthesis at the F6P node by dynamically repressing pfkA and/or activating glmS.
experiments.host: E. coli DN5 (DH5alpha derivative, delta-nag delta-ackA delta-poxB delta-ldhA delta-nan; constructed in previous studies - background)

interventions.description: Genomic replacement of pfkA promoter in DN5 with Ppam (pL19) or Ppar (pL25), yielding DN5-IM and DN5-PM.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 yes (two promoter strengths compared for this second product context).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Same dynamic-control strategy transferred to a second pathway context.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Lower glycolysis is a competitive pathway for GlcNAc synthesis from glucose; F6P is the shared precursor, so pfkA must be down-regulated.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured GlcNAc titers, growth and glucose consumption for DN5-IM/DN5-PM vs DN5.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit node-competition mechanism stated for F6P between glycolysis and GlcNAc pathway.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a product draws fructose-6-phosphate as precursor in glucose-grown E. coli, dynamically repress pfkA with an FBP-negative-response promoter, because this diverts F6P from lower glycolysis to the product while preserving early growth. (Validated for GlcNAc in the DN5 background.)

interventions.description: Plasmid-based dynamic activation of glmS using positive-response promoters PM23107 (pBacm) and PR23107-cra plus cra/P23102 (pBacar), transformed into DN5 to give DN5-GM and DN5-GAR.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 yes (two activation architectures compared; FBP-responsiveness of glmS activation verified).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Metabolite-responsive up-regulation of the product-forming enzyme (F6P aminotransferase).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: glmS needs up-regulation for GlcNAc overproduction, but early-stage overexpression may cause bacterial lysis and growth inhibition (Deng et al. 2005), so constitutive strong expression is unsuitable.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured GlcNAc titers for DN5-GM (6.33 g/L) and DN5-GAR (7.98 g/L) vs DN5 (0.46 g/L).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic need (F6P aminotransferase flux) combined with explicit literature-based toxicity concern (Deng et al. 2005) motivating timed activation.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When overexpression of a product-pathway enzyme is toxic in early growth (e.g., glmS in E. coli), drive it with a positive-response biosensor promoter activated as FBP accumulates, because induction is delayed until the production phase, avoiding lysis. (Validated for GlcNAc in DN5.)

interventions.description: Simultaneous dynamic repression of pfkA and activation of glmS (pBacm or pBacar into DN5-IM), yielding DN5-IMM and DN5-IMAR.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 yes (tests whether dual control exceeds single regulation - a design-relevant negative/comparative result).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Layered dual dynamic regulation at one metabolic node.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Hypothesis that combining both arms of node control (repress competitor + activate product path) would further raise GlcNAc titer.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured titer DN5-IMM 8.63 g/L vs single-regulation strains; FBP levels measured in DN5/DN5-IM/DN5-GAR/DN5-IMM.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Push-pull node engineering rationale explicitly described in Fig. 6A narrative.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When single dynamic repression of pfkA already restores most of the achievable F6P-to-GlcNAc flux in E. coli DN5, adding dynamic glmS activation on top gives no obvious further titer gain, because the node flux is already saturated by competitor repression. (Observed only in this DN5/GlcNAc context; do not generalize.)

experiments.conditions: Glucose as sole carbon source; shake-flask production implied; detailed conditions unknown (Methods absent; Supplementary Fig. 8 unavailable).
experiments.readouts: GlcNAc titer; growth; glucose consumption; intracellular FBP.
experiments.analysis: Titer/growth comparison; FBP-level interpretation per strain.
experiments.outcome: DN5-IM 8.65 g/L; DN5-GM 6.33; DN5-GAR 7.98; DN5-IMM 8.63 g/L; dual regulation not obviously higher than single; FBP lower in DN5-IM/DN5-IMM, unchanged in DN5-GAR. DN5-IMAR titer not reported in available text.
